description: The entire verse describing the departure from Hazeroth and camping in Paran is not present in the provided OSMAIN text (which starts at v1 with God speaking to Moses).
The entire verse 'Or Moïse dit aux enfants d'Israël tout ce que l'Éternel lui avait commandé.' is extra content not found in OSMAIN. OSMAIN begins directly with Moses addressing the tribal heads.

The verse 'David se leva donc et s'en alla, et Jonathan rentra dans la ville.' exists in the translation but is not found in the provided OSMAIN text (which ends at verse 42). This indicates the OSMAIN source text provided is truncated or this specific ending is missing from it.

Entire verse content: 'Puis David monta de là, et demeura dans les lieux forts d'En-Guédi.' This event (David moving to En-Gedi) is not present in the OSMAIN text provided, which starts with Saul's return.
The translation cuts off at 'ma', but the content implies the full sentence found in OSMAIN v4. No *extra* content beyond OSMAIN, just incomplete.
Translation cuts off at 'mai'. Content matches OSMAIN v10 up to the cut-off point.
Translation cuts off at 'en '. Content matches OSMAIN v11 up to the cut-off point.

The translation includes a final verse (v13) stating: 'Car toi, Éternel, tu bénis le juste; tu l'environnes de ta bienveillance comme d'un bouclier.' This text is completely absent from the provided OSMAIN text which ends at verse 12.

The title 'Hymne de David, qu'il chanta à l'Éternel, au sujet de Cush, le Benjamite' is present in Translation v1. In OSMAIN, this text exists as the first sentence of v1 ('En shiggajon av David...'), but the translation splits the title and the prayer body into two separate verses (v1 and v2), whereas OSMAIN keeps them together in v1.

The word 'Sélah (pause)' is explicitly written out with the parenthetical explanation '(pause)'. OSMAIN v5 only contains 'Sela' without the explanatory text. This is a minor extra content addition in the translation.
The parenthetical interpretation '(la mort du fils)' added to 'Sur Muth-Labben'.
The phrase 'plus que des ruines!' (more than ruins) which expands on the OSMAIN text.
The explanatory note '(Jeu d'instruments. Pause)' added to the musical terms.
Entire verse: 'Éternel, répands sur eux la terreur; que les peuples sachent qu'ils ne sont que des hommes! (Sélah.)' This content is completely absent from the OSMAIN text.
The title 'Au maître-chantre. Psaume de David. Sur Shéminith.' appears in Translation v1 but is only the first half of OSMAIN v1. The second half (the prayer) is missing from v1 and moved to v2.

The phrase 'je mettrai en sûreté celui qu'on insulte' (I will set in safety him who is insulted) differs significantly from OSMAIN v5's ending 'Jeg vil gi frelse til den som lengter etter det' (I will give salvation to the one who longs for it). The translation introduces the concept of being 'insulted' which is not explicitly present in the Norwegian text.

The phrase 'sauve le roi' (save the king) appears in Translation v10. The corresponding OSMAIN v9 says 'HERRE, frels oss!' (Lord, save us!). The translation has inserted 'the king' where the source text said 'us'. This is an addition of specific content not found in the OSMAIN text.

The translation includes a final verse (v14) that is completely absent from the OSMAIN text provided. The OSMAIN text ends at v13 ('...med dine buestrenger sikter du mot deres ansikter.'), while the translation adds: 'Élève-toi, ô Éternel, dans ta force! Nous chanterons et nous célébrons ta puissance!' (Arise, O Lord, in your strength! We will sing and praise your power!). This indicates the OSMAIN source text is missing this concluding verse found in standard Bible versions of Psalm 21.
Afin que ma gloire chante ta louange, et ne se taise point.
Éternel, mon Dieu, je te célébrerai à toujours.
The entire verse 'Hâte-toi, viens à mon aide, Seigneur, qui es ma délivrance!' is present in the translation but missing from the OSMAIN text. The OSMAIN text concludes at verse 22.
The entire verse 14 ('Détourne de moi ton regard, et que je reprenne mes forces...') is present in the French translation but completely missing from the OSMAIN text provided.
Title: 'Au maître-chantre. Cantique des enfants de Coré.' (To the chief musician. A Psalm of the sons of Korah). This text is completely absent from OSMAIN v1.
Je rendrai ton nom célèbre dans tous les âges; aussi les peuples t'honoreront à toujours, à perpétuité. (I will make your name famous in all ages; so the peoples will honor you forever and ever.)
Explicit definition '(jeunes filles)' for 'Alamoth'.
Phrase 'et fort aisé à trouver' (and very easy to find) is added to the description of God's help.

The phrase 'nous avons attendu ta faveur' (we have waited for your favor) in Translation v10 does not match the OSMAIN text 'Vi har fordypet oss i din trofaste kjærlighet' (We have meditated on/thought deeply about your faithful love). The concept of 'waiting/expecting' is an addition not present in the source.
The entire verse is a superscription/title not present as a separate numbered verse in OSMAIN. In OSMAIN, this text is part of the introduction to v1.
Title and historical context: 'Au maître-chantre. Maskil (cantique) de David; Lorsque Doëg, l'Iduméen, vint avertir Saül...'
Continuation of historical context: 'et lui dit que David s'était rendu dans la maison d'Achimélec.'

The entire verse 'Au maître-chantre. Sur la flûte. Cantique de David.' is present in the translation but has no corresponding text in the OSMAIN master text, which starts directly with the body of the psalm.
Title and musical instructions: 'Au maître-chantre. Cantique de David, avec les instruments à cordes;'
Added emotional descriptor: 'avec joie' (with joy) in the phrase regarding seeing enemies.

The entire verse 24 ('Toi, ô Dieu, tu les précipiteras au fond de la fosse; les hommes de sang et de fraude n'atteindront pas la moitié de leurs jours; mais moi, je me confie en toi.') is present in the translation but completely missing from the OSMAIN text provided. The OSMAIN text concludes at verse 23.
Superscription/Title text (Au maître-chantre... devant Saül) is present in the translation as verse 1 but is unnumbered header text in OSMAIN.
Phrase: 'jusqu'à ce que les calamités soient passées' (until the calamities have passed). This phrase appears at the end of v2 in the translation but is absent from OSMAIN v1.
The translation stops mid-sentence at 'étendard', missing 'to lift high, for the sake of truth. Selah' found in Osmain v5.
The text ends with 'car' (for), which is a conjunction leading into the next verse, indicating a split rather than extra content, but the sentence is incomplete without v14.

The translation introduces the specific categories 'Les petits' (the little ones) and 'les grands' (the great ones) and explicitly states they are 'néant' (nothing), whereas OSMAIN v9 uses 'menneskers barn' (children of men) and 'fornemme menns sønner' (sons of noble men) with the descriptors 'pust' (breath) and 'løgn' (lie). The translation expands the text by interpreting 'children of men' as 'little ones' and equating them to 'nothing', which is an interpretative addition not present in the literal OSMAIN wording.
Phrase 'au point du jour' (at daybreak) is present in translation but absent in OSMAIN v2.
Phrase 'pour te suivre' (to follow you) is present in translation but absent in OSMAIN v9.
The phrase 'Nous voilà prêts; le plan est formé!' (We are ready; the plan is formed!) appears in the translation but has no corresponding text in OSMAIN v7.

The phrase 'et les roues de ton char distillent l'abondance' (and the wheels of your chariot drip abundance) appears in Translation v12. The corresponding OSMAIN v11 only mentions 'dine spor drypper av overflod' (your tracks/footprints drip with abundance). The specific reference to 'chariot wheels' is an addition in the translation.
The phrase 'le dominateur' (the ruler/dominator) appears in French but is not present in the Norwegian text ('som leder dem' - who leads them). While semantically similar, it is an explicit addition.
The phrase 'les cieux éternels' (the eternal heavens) is added to the description of the heavens in French, whereas Norwegian only says 'de eldgamle himlers himmel' (heaven of ancient heavens).

The imperative 'Rendez la force à Dieu!' (Give strength to God) differs from OSMAIN's 'Gi Gud ære!' (Give God glory). Additionally, the French v35 omits the final clauses of OSMAIN v35 ('Fryktinngytende er du... Lovet være Gud!'), which are moved to v36.

Complete verse not found in OSMAIN. Content: 'La race de ses serviteurs l'aura pour héritage; ceux qui aiment son nom, y auront leur demeure.' (The seed of his servants shall inherit it; those who love his name shall dwell therein.)

The entire verse 'Au maître-chantre. Psaume de David; pour servir de mémorial.' is extra content relative to the OSMAIN text provided, as OSMAIN v1 starts immediately with the prayer 'For korlederen... Gud, fri meg ut!' without a separate title verse.

The phrase 'des ravisseurs' (of the robbers) in 'plus que les montagnes des ravisseurs' is not present in OSMAIN v4 ('de evige fjellene' - of the eternal mountains). This changes the meaning significantly.

The entire verse 'Tu as conduit ton peuple comme un troupeau, par la main de Moïse et d'Aaron' is present in the translation but completely absent from the provided OSMAIN text (which ends at verse 20). This suggests the OSMAIN source text provided is incomplete or follows a numbering scheme where this content is merged into v20 or omitted. In standard Hebrew numbering, Psalm 77:21 often includes this shepherd imagery.

The translation includes verse 19: 'Et qu'ils connaissent que toi seul, qui t'appelles l'Éternel, tu es le souverain de toute la terre.' (And let them know that you alone, whose name is the Lord, are the Most High over all the earth). This text is completely absent from the provided OSMAIN text.

The entire first verse of the translation (Superscription: 'Au maître-chantre. Psaume des enfants de Coré, sur Guitthith.') is missing from the OSMAIN text provided. The OSMAIN text starts directly with the poetic content in v1.
The translation includes verse 14 ('La justice marchera devant lui...') which is completely missing from the OSMAIN text provided. The OSMAIN text ends at verse 13.

The phrase 'sur la cithare' (on the lyre) appears in Translation v1 but is not present in OSMAIN v1. OSMAIN v1 mentions 'Etter «Mahalat leannot»' which is a musical instruction, but does not explicitly name the instrument 'cithare'. This is an addition in the French translation.

The translation includes a final verse (v14) that is completely absent from the provided OSMAIN text. The OSMAIN text concludes at v13 with 'for menneskelig hjelp er forgjeves.' The translation adds: 'Nous ferons des actions de valeur en Dieu, et il foulera nos ennemis.' This indicates the OSMAIN source text provided is incomplete compared to this specific French translation (likely Oester version of Psalm 108).
The entire verse is extra content not found in OSMAIN. It contains the exhortation to 'rejoice in your youth' and warnings about vanity before the command to remember the Creator.
The entire verse is extra content not found in OSMAIN. It continues the warning about banishing sorrow and states that youth is vanity.
Text cuts off mid-sentence: '...se répandra par-dessu'. The sentence is incomplete compared to OSMAIN v7.
Text cuts off mid-sentence: '...s'adressera-t-il aux mor'. The sentence is incomplete compared to OSMAIN v19.

Entire verse present in translation but missing from OSMAIN source. Content: 'Mais il ne fera pas toujours sombre... couvrira de gloire la [terre]'. This appears to be a continuation or an addition not found in the provided Norwegian master text.

Complete verse addressing the children of Ammon and their reproach, stating the sword is drawn for slaughter against them. This entire section (v33-v37) appears to be missing from the provided OSMAIN text which ends at v32.
Continuation of judgment on Ammon regarding false visions and lying omens, casting them upon the dead wicked.
Command to return the sword to its sheath and judgment in the place of origin.
Declaration of pouring out indignation and fire, delivering them into the hands of barbarous men.
Final declaration that they will become prey to fire, their blood will flow, and they will be forgotten.

The entire verse: 'Éphraïm m'a environné de mensonge, et la maison d'Israël de tromperie; et Juda est encore inconstant avec Dieu, avec le Saint, le Fidèle.' This content is completely absent from the OSMAIN text provided.

Entire verse missing from OSMAIN: 'Et l'Éternel prépara un grand poisson pour engloutir Jonas, et Jonas fut dans le ventre du poisson trois jours et trois nuits.' (The Lord prepared a great fish to swallow Jonah, and Jonah was in the belly of the fish three days and three nights).

Phrase added/expanded: 'abandonnent celui qui leur fait miséricorde' (abandon the one who shows them mercy). The OSMAIN text only says they turn their backs on 'grace that could have been theirs', not that they abandon God directly.
Translation adds 'et le jeûne' (and fasting) to the instruction on driving out demons. OSMAIN v29 only mentions prayer ('ved bønn').
Translation adds 'et toute oblation sera salée de sel' (and every offering will be salted with salt). OSMAIN v49 only mentions being salted with fire.
Translation includes 'ne commets point de fraude' (do not commit fraud) which is absent in OSMAIN v19.
Translation adds the phrase 'à ceux qui se confient dans les richesses' (to those who trust in riches), expanding the meaning beyond OSMAIN v24.
Translation includes 'ou femme' (or wife) in the list of relatives left behind, which is not present in OSMAIN v29.
